summary: An automated pricing, allocation, ranking, offer, fee, commission, credit, insurance, employment, platform, or commercial decision process uses an observed or inferred vulnerability, urgency, dependency, constrained-choice state, reduced practical alternatives, financial pressure, behavioural susceptibility, or comparable protected signal to individualise or worsen an economic term in order to extract additional value from the affected person or organisation.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: Dynamic or differentiated pricing is not inherently a governance failure. The governance boundary is crossed when a signal that should trigger protection, minimisation, accommodation, neutral treatment, or heightened scrutiny is instead used as an optimisation input for extraction. A person's urgency, distress, dependency, diminished alternatives, financial pressure, capacity constraint, or comparable vulnerability should not become a reason to charge them more, offer them worse terms, reduce their practical ability to refuse, or otherwise convert vulnerability into commercial leverage. CAM therefore needs a distinction between legitimate market-responsive pricing and vulnerability-conditioned personalised extraction, with provenance for the signals used, counterfactual visibility, contestability, and protections against incompatible repurposing of vulnerability data.
evidence_confidence: high mechanism-level confidence; provider-specific implementation and causal pricing inputs remain claim-relative and may be disputed

source_records.source_title: FTC Surveillance Pricing Study Indicates Wide Range of Personal Data Used to Set Individualized Consumer Prices
source_records.system_or_product: surveillance-pricing intermediaries and retailer pricing systems
source_records.deployment_context: Consumer pricing systems using personal characteristics and behavioural data to tailor prices and promotions.
source_records.source_context: FTC staff reported that surveillance-pricing intermediaries and retailers can use precise location, demographics, browsing patterns, shopping history, mouse movements and other consumer data to target different consumers with different prices or promotions.
source_records.relevance_note: Direct regulator evidence that personal and behavioural data are used in the market to individualise economic terms. It supports the general mechanism but does not by itself establish that every personalised price exploits vulnerability.

primary_artefact_access.access_method: Direct review of the public FTC publication.
limitations: The FTC publication is an initial staff perspective from a market study rather than an adjudication of any named retailer's conduct.
Personalised pricing can have benign or consumer-beneficial forms; the VIGIL failure threshold requires incompatible use of vulnerability or constrained-choice signals for extraction.

source_records.interpretive_reliance: Used to establish that personal and behavioural signals are operational inputs to individualised pricing systems and therefore can create a governance pathway for vulnerability-conditioned extraction.

source_records.relevance_note: Official evidence of the governance concern that inferred susceptibility or maximum willingness to pay can become an input to individualised pricing. The inquiry is not treated as a finding that every named company uses those inputs.

limitations: A congressional investigation request establishes scrutiny and alleged mechanisms, not final factual findings about a named provider.

source_records.interpretive_reliance: Used to distinguish ordinary market-responsive pricing from the narrower concern that personal susceptibility or constrained-choice signals are used to increase extraction.

contextual_relations.rationale: FM-0074 concerns authority for secondary use of data. FM-0075 concerns the downstream decision mechanism in which vulnerability or constrained-choice signals are used to worsen economic terms. Either can occur without the other.

failure_mode_definition: A failure mode in which an automated or algorithmically mediated decision process uses an observed or inferred vulnerability, urgency, dependency, reduced practical alternatives, financial pressure, capacity constraint, behavioural susceptibility, emotional state, or comparable signal that should trigger protection, minimisation, accommodation, neutral treatment, or heightened scrutiny as an input for personalising, ranking, allocating, or worsening an economic term in order to increase extraction, margin, conversion, retention, or equivalent commercial advantage. The failure is not differential pricing itself; it is the incompatible repurposing of vulnerability or constrained-choice information as commercial leverage.
failure_threshold: The threshold is met when: (1) the system has access to, infers, or operationally derives a vulnerability, urgency, dependency, reduced-alternative, financial-pressure, capacity, susceptibility, emotional-state, or comparable protected signal about an affected actor; (2) that signal should materially support protection, minimisation, accommodation, neutral treatment, or heightened scrutiny in the relevant context; (3) the signal instead materially conditions an economic term, ranking, allocation, promotion, fee, commission, eligibility decision, or offer in a direction that increases extraction or worsens the affected actor's position; and (4) the commercial optimisation purpose is incompatible with the protective significance of the signal. Market-wide supply-and-demand pricing, transparent time-or-distance pricing, ordinary cost-based differentiation, or personalisation that does not exploit vulnerability or constrained choice does not satisfy the threshold.

harm_vectors: repurposing of protected or sensitive signals
failure_classification.likelihood: structurally evidenced across surveillance-pricing markets; provider-specific use of vulnerability inputs varies and may be contested
failure_classification.confidence: high mechanism confidence; provider-specific causal inputs remain claim-relative
affected_rights_or_interests: access to essential or time-sensitive services
failure_classification.failure_scope: algorithmic economic decisions that repurpose vulnerability or constrained-choice signals toward extraction
failure_classification.recurrence_pattern: can recur wherever personal or behavioural profiling is coupled to pricing, promotions, eligibility, fees, commissions, allocation, or other commercial optimisation
failure_classification.persistence: can persist through behavioural profiles, pricing models, experimentation systems, customer segmentation, inferred willingness-to-pay models, and downstream decision pipelines
failure_classification.reproducibility: testable through controlled counterfactual comparisons that vary vulnerability or constrained-choice signals while holding legitimate market and cost variables constant
failure_classification.visibility: often low because affected people generally cannot see the profile, pricing inputs, counterfactual price, or price offered to comparable users
failure_classification.severity_assessment_basis: S2 reflects potentially material recurring economic harm and agency impairment, especially where affected people have reduced alternatives or depend on time-sensitive or essential services, without treating every instance of differentiated pricing as severe harm.
failure_classification.severity_assessment_gap: Prevalence, provider-specific inputs, magnitude of individual economic harm, protected-class effects, competition effects, and jurisdiction-specific legality vary and require occurrence-level evidence.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: The defined mechanism is the repurposing of vulnerability, capacity, emotional, financial-pressure or comparable protected signals away from protection or minimisation and toward personalised commercial optimisation. That is the canonical mechanism of Protected-Signal Influence Repurposing. Differential pricing based only on market conditions is expressly excluded.

review_history.reviewer_platform: OpenAI ChatGPT with web and GitHub access
review_history.review_scope: Review the current post-consolidation VIGIL taxonomy for a failure mechanism covering vulnerability-conditioned algorithmic pricing and determine whether a new class is required.
known_limitations: The review did not inspect proprietary pricing models or internal provider telemetry.
Consumer Reports observed price differences but did not establish that a specific vulnerability signal caused each difference.
Uber expressly denies using personal data, protected characteristics, phone battery levels, phone models or similar device information to personalise base prices.
The FTC market study establishes ecosystem-level personalised-pricing practices but does not establish the conduct of every named provider.
review_history.review_outcome: No new Failure Class is required. The missing VIGIL layer was a Failure Mode. The mechanism maps cleanly to FC-000050 Protected-Signal Influence Repurposing because the qualifying condition is incompatible reuse of vulnerability or comparable protected signals toward economic extraction. FC-000052 is not assigned by default because transparent price differentiation can exploit a protected signal without separately establishing deception, coercion, persistence or another instrumental choice-manipulation tactic.
